description: A place the person holds, lives in, keeps returning to or is working toward — a home, a property, a town, a region, a country, an airport, a venue, or a PART of a home or property (its roof, its workshop, a bedroom). One node per place at any grain, with `kind` saying which and `parent_ref` giving the hierarchy (Workshop → Casa in Catral → Catral → Alicante → Spain) without a second schema. Minted because the platform has no entity for a place: its `location` is a single visit whose `place_ref` points at exactly this, and every other place field on the gateway is a bare string. Cited by id from properties, goals, ends, decisions, trips, organizations, events and facts (edges: located_at, lives_at, part_of, fact_about). What is TRUE of a place — its nearest airport, its tax regime — is a `fact` node that points at it, never a field on it. Never deleted; `suspended` retires, as people are retired. v2 (2026-09-24) adds the `part` grain, `part_type`, a house's `drawing`, and declares `coords_source` / `coords_label`.

address.description: The address as written, for a home or a property — 'Casa in Catral, Alicante, Spain'. Null above that grain.
address.title: Address

aliases.description: The other names it goes by in their words — 'the Spanish house', 'Casa in Catral'. What dedupe rests on: a name that folds to one of these is this place, and the room never mints a twin.
aliases.title: Aliases

coords_label.description: The gazetteer's words for the position — 'Catral, Alicante, Spain — its town, not its address'.
coords_label.title: Position label

coords_source.description: `given` pasted by the person, `chosen` picked by them from the finder's candidates, `found` placed by the finder on its own. Never set on a `part`.
coords_source.title: Where the position came from

drawing.description: For a `home` or `property` only: how its page draws it. Null reads as `house`.
drawing.title: Drawing

kind.description: The grain: `home` where they live, `property` a place they hold, `part` a part of a home or property (it sits inside one by `parent_ref` and has no position or address of its own), then the geography above it. A country or a region is a place of that kind, never a schema of its own.
kind.title: Kind

minted_for.description: The id of the node this place was first read off — a property row, a goal, a decision — so a retraction there can find what it made.
minted_for.title: Minted for

name.description: What they call it — 'Catral', 'Spain', 'Casa in Catral'. The title of the node says the same.
name.title: Name

parent_ref.description: The id of the place this one sits in — a part's house, the house's town, the town's region, the region's country. Mirrored by the `part_of` edge; this field is the read-side truth.
parent_ref.title: Part of

part_type.description: For a `part` only: which part of the house it is, and so where it is drawn — `living` the living room, `front` the facade (shutters, windows, door), `systems` what runs the house (cooling, heating, electrics, water). Null for every other kind.
part_type.title: Part type

source_phrase.description: The words of theirs the place was read out of, when a reading minted it.
source_phrase.title: Source phrase

source_ref.description: Stable per mint — 'allocations:place:<kind>:<folded name>[:<folded country>]', and for a part 'allocations:place:part:<house id>:<part type>:<folded name>' so two houses' roofs are never one node — so a retried create is a retry, not a second node.
source_ref.title: Source ref

status.description: `suspended` retires a place — a property sold, a home left — without deleting what cited it.
status.title: Status
